parsed_answer.content:
Polymorphism, literally meaning 'many forms', is a foundational pillar of Object-Oriented Programming that allows a single interface to represent multiple underlying implementations. In Java, polymorphism splits fundamentally into two axes: compile-time polymorphism (static binding) and runtime polymorphism (dynamic binding). Compile-time polymorphism is achieved via method overloading, where multiple methods share the same identifier within a class but maintain distinct parameter lists. The compiler determines which method to execute during compilation by inspecting method signatures, ensuring strict type safety without dynamic dispatch overhead.

Conversely, runtime polymorphism relies on method overriding and dynamic method dispatch. This mechanism allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method that is already defined in its parent class. The JVM resolves the method invocation at runtime based on the actual object type residing in the heap, rather than the reference type declared in code. Understanding the interplay between compile-time resolution and runtime dispatch is critical for architecting extensible systems, designing decoupled interfaces, and leveraging design patterns like Strategy, Template Method, and Factory.

items: Method overloading resolution is handled strictly by the Java compiler (javac) using static type analysis. If an exact parameter match is not found, the compiler uses widening primitive conversions, boxing/unboxing, and variablearity (varargs) rules in a specific precedence order.

Runtime polymorphism operates via the JVM's dynamic method dispatch. Every loaded class maintains a virtual method table (vtable) in the metaspace. When a polymorphic method is invoked via invokevirtual, the JVM uses the object's class pointer to index into the vtable and locate the correct implementation address.

Overriding rules dictate that the overriding method must not reduce visibility, must have a compatible return type (covariance is permitted), and cannot throw broader checked exceptions than the overridden method.

parsed_answer.content: A common interview trap and production bug source involves attempting to 'override' static methods. Static methods are bound at compile-time based on the reference type, not the runtime object type. If a subclass defines a static method with the exact same signature as a superclass static method, it is method hiding, not overriding. Polymorphism does not apply to static methods or private methods, meaning dynamic dispatch will fail silently if you rely on reference polymorphism for utility methods.

title: Polymorphism — compile-time vs runtime, method overloading vs overriding
